text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn Friday met Young Democrat president Viktor Orban, chairman of Parliament's European integration committee, to discuss Hungary's planned accession to NATO and the European Union.
- Smallholder president Jozsef Torgyan accused the Young Democrats Friday of being behind the idea of a merger between the parliamentary groups of the Democratic Forum and Christian Democrats.
- Free Democrats ruled out any electoral alliance before the first round of parliamentary elections next May.
- A Eurpoean Commission report on Hungary is expected to speak positively about the country.
- The EU-Hungarian associate parliamentary committee is holding a session in Budapest May 20-22.

- Slovakia's Minister of Transport Jan Jasovsky said Bratislava will not hold negotiations with Budapest on the reconstruction of a bridge over the Danube at the Hungarian-Slovak border near Esztergom.
- The Malaysian royal couple, King Tuanku Jaafar and his wife, arrive in Hungary today on a five-day official visit.
- Speaker of Parliament Zoltan Gal opened five days of talks in Beijing Sunday.
- Inflation may drop to single-digit levels by 1999, while the EU-required rate could be reached by 2005 a Finance Ministry official said.
- The balance of payments closed February some $198 million in the red, a far cry from the $313 million registered a year earlier, the National Bank (MNB) reports.
- Retail trade turnover shrank by 4.7% in March, and by 10% in the first quarter in real terms compared to the same period of 1996.
NEPSZABADSAG
- A French research has described the Smallholders, the Hungarian Justice and Life Party (MIEP) and a small group of skinheads headed by Neo-Nazi Albert Szabo as "extremist groups" in Hungary.

- Thousands of Catholic faithful visited the Mariaremete shrine on the outskirts of Budapest Monday morning after vandals pushed over seven reliefs depicting the Stages of the Cross and a statue of the Virgin Mary.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Sweden's Electrolux will boost the equity capital of refrigerator maker Lehel Hutogepgyar Kft. by 6 billion forints.
- Performance in the construction industry is likely to increase further this year.
- The state lottery and gambling company Szerencsejatek Rt. generated 3.3 billion forints pre-tax profits in 1996, Ft 500 million more than in the previous year.
